decision: The page opens on the one open problem: when it started, who it affects, which SLO it breaks and how fast the budget burns
why: On-call engineers arrive from a page; the first screen must answer 'how bad and since when' before any chart.
value: Triage starts in seconds, and MTTR fell from 2–3 h to 30–45 min in the system this is modeled on.

decision: The service flow is discovered from trace parent/child spans, with health rings from apdex; the unhealthy node pulses
why: Hand-drawn maps go stale; spans already say who calls whom.
value: The map is always true, and the broken hop is obvious.

decision: Latency (p50/p95/p99) and throughput are separate one-axis charts sharing a time range, with the deploy marker on both
why: Two measures on two scales mislead on one chart; the marker lines the cause up with the effect.
value: The question 'did the deploy do this?' is answered by looking.

decision: The AI root cause cites the deploy, the traces and the config diff, and offers the two fixes as buttons a person presses
why: Diagnosis is where AI saves time; remediation stays a human decision with a trace of its own.
value: Fixes are one click, reviewed, and every system recovers together.

decision: Tidewatch reads the same in-browser world as every zone: faults open problems, fixes close them
why: A hosted APM per visitor is money; the simulation keeps signals, traces and logs consistent at $0.
alternative: Static screenshots of a real APM.
value: Chaos in one tab is a problem here, a banner in Counter and slower scoring in Pay.
